goals.goal: The 8-person internal team and the external payment sub-processor act only on documented instructions from TinyTask as controller (or as processor for customer task data) and remain bound by a confidentiality obligation; no authentication-strength threshold is imposed by this obligation — the surrounding instruction-and-confidentiality architecture is the operative duty.
goals.adjustment: Restated from the GDPR Sub-SO staff-side obligation for an 8-employee SaaS controller/processor with one external sub-processor; the "documented instructions" chain is scoped to the internal team plus the payment sub-processor rather than a large enterprise hierarchy; the absence of an authentication-strength threshold is preserved verbatim from the OJ.

goals.goal: When a customer's own user (data subject) exercises a GDPR right through the customer (controller), TinyTask as processor verifies the requester's identity using reasonable means proportionate to the risk of mis-identification, given the non-sensitive, small-scale B2B data context.
goals.adjustment: Restated from the GDPR Sub-SO data-subject-side verification obligation; proportionality is anchored to the fact-sheet context (non-sensitive data, B2B SaaS, 8 employees) rather than a generic enterprise scale; the verification trigger is "reasonable doubt" per Art. 12(6), not a blanket MFA mandate.

goals.goal: The TinyTask SaaS product (web and mobile interface, default class, self-assessment conformity) protects against unauthorised access through appropriate control mechanisms — which may include authentication, identity, or access-management systems — commensurate with the identified cybersecurity risk of the product; the mechanism choice is at the manufacturer's discretion under the 3-way OR.
goals.adjustment: Restated from the CRA Sub-SO for a default-class SaaS product with individual customer logins; the "may include" permissive language is preserved verbatim from the OJ; no MFA or continuous-authentication phrase is imposed; the risk-assessment anchor is scoped to the product's default-class self-assessment conformity procedure.
